$comment: This site's own facts, as data: which pack is the ground, which mode a visitor
gets who has never chosen, and the set of sites the family's menu moves between.
A pack identifier is a token, and this file is the one place a site picks one, so
a renamed or retired pack is a compile error rather than a page that quietly
inherits the ground. The data-system records the page ground and a product's mark
as two different axes: the ground is stable for the life of the page, and a
product's mark comes from this directory.
These five records are read by two independent readers, which is why they are here
and not in a module: the bar's menu takes them, and the pack-boundary gate reads
this file the way it reads the pack map the bar is checked against. What changed
about them is when they paint rather than what they are: the family is a menu now,
so a closed menu draws no mark at all, and the four packs that are not this site's
ground are no longer above the fold of any page. The menu shows the same five, on
the same terms, the moment a reader opens it.
